extracted.intended_audience: researchers, NIH extramural community, policy analysts, and academics studying grant-funding disparities
extracted.subtask_description: Quantitative analysis of NIH R01 (de novo and resubmission) applications to determine how topic choice, Institute/Center (IC) assignment, and peer review outcomes relate to racial (AAB) funding disparities; includes regression modelling, sensitivity checks, and policy discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: AAB Preferred topic (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: We designated a topic as 'AAB Preferred' if it was among the 16 topics that accounted for 50% of AAB applications. (In different analyses the count/percentage differed slightly: e.g., 11% of topics accounted for 50% of AAB applications in resubmissions / single-PI analyses.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper uses a 50% cutoff to define AAB-preferred topics but also (in revision) treats AAB preference as a continuous variable (Equation 1) and reports sensitivity analyses (e.g., using a 70% cut-point) to show findings are robust. Reviewers request a rationale for cutoffs and that sensitivity be reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review 'Discussed' status (first hurdle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether an application 'made it past the first hurdle of peer review', i.e., reaching the point of formal discussion (labeled 'Discussed').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a binary outcome/metric (probability of discussion, e.g., Equation 5). The manuscript notes AAB-preferred-topic applications were more likely to be discussed, and examines topic-level probability of discussion vs proportion of AAB applications (scatter plots, p-values reported).

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority Score (mean/median priority score)
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority score assigned to discussed applications; lower mean priority scores correspond to better, more favorable reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topic-level mean priority scores (Equation 6) are analyzed and plotted against AAB preference; medians and IQRs are reported in tables. Analyses find no association of mean priority score with proportion of AAB applications (non-significant p-values reported).

rubrics_metrics.name: Percentile ranking
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentile ranking of application priority scores (reported as median and IQR in descriptive tables).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as descriptive summary of peer review outcomes alongside priority scores and 'Discussed' status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awarded / Award rate (funding success)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether an application was awarded (funded); overall award rates reported (e.g., <10% for first-time de novo; 30% for resubmissions; 9% for single-PI de novo).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IC-specific award rates are a central explanatory variable: the authors report that IC-specific award rates explain racial disparities to a greater degree than topic choice. Models include IC award rate as a predictor; reviewers request reporting award rates stratified by PI race per IC.

rubrics_metrics.name: IC Award Rate (Institute/Center-specific award rate)
rubrics_metrics.description: The award rate specific to each NIH Institute or Center (IC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IC award rate is strongly associated with likelihood of funding (positive regression coefficient, p<0.001) and, when included in models, reduces the absolute regression coefficient for AAB PI (i.e., explains part of the disparity). Reviewers ask for IC funding ecology context (e.g., average amounts allocated to each IC) and for per-IC award rates by race.

rubrics_metrics.name: IC assignment process / receipt and referral
rubrics_metrics.description: How Institute assignments are made: applicants may include keywords or request a specific IC, but assignment is performed by CSR and may not always respect applicant requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer requests: discuss details of assignment (applicant request vs CSR assignment), percent of applications that go directly to Institutes (RFAs) vs CSR, whether applications are reassigned on resubmission, role of dual-assignments and selection/refusal to pick up as secondary IC, and whether AA/B applications are differentially assigned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regression model covariates (variables included)
rubrics_metrics.description: Variables used in probit regression models include: AAB Preferred Topic, IC Award Rate, AAB Principal Investigator indicator, Early Stage Investigator, Multi-PI Application, Human Subjects, Animal Subjects. Models reported as Model 1 (univariable), Model 2 (topic + IC award rate), Model 3 (adds ESI, multi-PI, human/animal subjects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model outputs include regression coefficients, standard errors, AIC, BIC, Log Likelihood, deviance, number of observations, and p-value significance. Authors explain coefficients and p-values in table legends and text; reviewers ask that results also be expressed in percent-of-disparity-explained terms for accessibility and comparison to prior work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early Stage Investigator status (covariate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicator for Early Stage Investigator (ESI) included in models; shown to have positive association with funding in models (e.g., regression coefficient positive, p<0.001).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer requests explicit definition of how 'Early-Stage investigator' was defined and whether seniority metrics (publications/h-index) correlate with IC assignment or funding success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-PI versus Single-PI application
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether an application included multiple PIs; analyses were performed both including all applications and restricted to single-PI applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors note multi-PI status may affect topic choice attribution and that analyses restricted to single-PI applications yielded similar findings. Reviewers request discussion of how multiple PIs influence topic selection and assignment, and whether contact PI vs co-PI roles matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission application inclusion/exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary analyses excluded resubmission applications and competing renewals; separate analyses repeated focusing on resubmissions (31,900 resubmissions; 30% award rate) and found similar findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer critique: justify excluding competing continuations given prior literature (Hoppe included them) and consider making full sample the main analysis or provide rationale and sensitivity analyses. Also request data on whether resubmissions return to same IC or are reassigned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and handling of topic-preference as continuous vs categorical
rubrics_metrics.description: AAB preference for each topic was calculated as a continuous variable (Equation 1) in revised analyses; earlier categorical approach identified topics accounting for 50% of AAB applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors present both categorical (50% cutoff) and continuous treatments and report that continuous-variable analyses reinforce absence of association between AAB preference and peer review outcomes. Reviewers pressed for justification of categorical cutoffs and for sensitivity checks (authors provided 70% cut-point results).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size and interpretive caveats for AAB PIs
rubrics_metrics.description: Only ~2% of PIs in the study were African American or Black (AAB), limiting the ability for that small group to cover the entire breadth of NIH-funded topics; small numbers are a source of error for describing AAB scientific interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors explicitly caution that analyses are of applications not persons and note limitations of small AAB sample size. Reviewers stress this limitation and request more recent data and expanded analyses where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting per-IC racial award rates (recommended)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer recommendation: report award rate for applications with AA/B versus white PIs listed per IC, instead of only aggregate award rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: a key claim hinges on presumption that within-IC racial success-rate ratios are similar; reviewers request explicit per-IC race-stratified award rates to verify claims and to assess whether disparities vary across ICs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide IC funding context / 'funding ecology' (recommended)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer recommendation: include columns showing average amount of money assigned to each IC across relevant fiscal years (and percentage), to contextualize differences in IC award rates and 'funding ecology'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to help readers understand why some ICs have lower award rates (e.g., small IC budgets like NIMHD/NINR) and to ground conclusions about assignment-driven disparities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice and justification of IC/topic grouping cutoffs
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer critique: authors used top-quartile of ICs (6/24) as 'AAB-preferred ICs' and 50% cutoff for topics, but provided little rationale; choices may be arbitrary and affect conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation to justify cutoff choices and show how alternative cutoffs (e.g., include DE, DA, MH) affect results; authors responded by presenting additional analyses and explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine white vs AA/B success rates across ICs (recommended analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer recommendation: primary analysis should examine white vs AA/B success rates within each IC to directly assess within-IC disparities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is proposed as a simpler and more direct test of whether IC assignment alone explains racial disparities; reviewers request such analyses be included or discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include/compare applications submitted directly to Institutes (RFA, P01, training grants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer asks whether numbers included are all R01s received or just those received by CSR; some R01s go directly to Institutes (e.g., RFAs), as do P01s and training grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation: report sub-analyses for applications that went directly to a specific IC vs CSR-assigned to assess differences in AAB funding rates by assignment pathway.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider dual-assignment and secondary IC pickup selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer requests analyses of whether applications are dual-assigned and whether selection/refusal to pick up as a secondary IC varies, and whether AAB applications are more/less likely to be dual-assigned or picked up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accounting for dual assignments and shared funding between ICs could affect observed award-rate patterns and explanations for disparities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control for PI seniority / bibliometrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer asks whether seniority (# publications, h-index) and funding success correlate with specific ICs and suggests controlling for these metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation: include PI-level covariates (productivity/fame metrics) to test whether topic choice/IC assignment or PI experience drive observed disparities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze prior submission/resubmission behavior by race
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer requests data on whether there were differences in number of applications submitted before successful funding for AAB investigators, or whether AAB investigators were less likely to submit an A1 resubmission after initial triage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understanding resubmission behavior could illuminate whether disparities arise from differential persistence or resubmission practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model diagnostics and transparent statistical reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Report model fit statistics (AIC, BIC, Log Likelihood, Deviance), number of observations, standard errors, and p-value thresholds; explain regression coefficients and p-values in text and table legends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors provided such diagnostics; reviewers request that results be expressed in more accessible terms (e.g., percent of disparity explained) for the general audience and comparability with prior literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and code availability (reproducibility standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors provided de-identified data frame (.RData) and R markdown files to reproduce the main paper and appendices (including all tables, figures, and numbers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows transparent reporting best-practices; reviewers and editors expect reproducible analyses and access to code/data for verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation caution: analyses of applications not persons
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors explicitly note this was an analysis of applications, not persons; multi-PI applications complicate attributions since all PIs influence topic choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation to be cautious in extrapolating from application-level findings to individual investigators or groups, and to discuss limitations accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss policy implications and potential remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer asks authors to discuss potential resolutions (e.g., IC set-asides for certain topic choices) and policy implications of finding that topic-to-IC assignment drives disparities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are asked to consider and discuss concrete policy options and implications rather than only descriptive findings.
